sections.title: 📘 Basic Concept
sections.content: The word 'Percent' comes from 'Per-Cent', which literally means 'out of 100'. Think of it as a way to express any number as a part of 100. The symbol used is '%'. For example, if you have 50%, it simply means you have 50 out of every 100 units.

sections.title: 💰 Percentage in Money (₹)
sections.content: In daily life, we use percentages to calculate discounts or taxes on prices. For example, if a T-shirt costs ₹1,000 and there is a 10% discount, you save ₹10 for every ₹100. Since there are ten 'hundreds' in ₹1,000, you save 10 x 10 = ₹100. You pay only ₹900.

sections.title: 📈 Increase and Decrease
sections.content: Percentage change tells us how much a value has gone up or down. ⬆️ Increase: If your pocket money of ₹100 is increased by 20%, you get ₹20 extra (Total ₹120). ⬇️ Decrease: If a ₹500 bag is on 50% sale, the price drops by half (Total ₹250). To find the new value, always find the percentage amount first and then add or subtract it from the original.

sections.title: 🧮 Important Formulas
sections.content:
1. To find a percentage: (Part / Total) × 100. 
2. To find the value of a percent: (Percent / 100) × Total. 
3. Fraction to Percent: Multiply the fraction by 100. 
4. Percent to Decimal: Divide the number by 100 (move decimal 2 places left).

sections.title: ⚠️ Common Mistakes
sections.content:
• Forgetting the Base: Always check what number you are taking a percentage of. 10% of ₹100 is not the same as 10% of ₹200. 
• Adding Percentages: You cannot simply add 10% and 10% off if they are applied one after another. 
• Ratio Confusion: Remember that 1:4 as a ratio means 1 out of 5 total parts (20%), not 1 out of 4 (25%).

sections.title: 📝 Quick Summary
sections.content:
• Percent means 'per 100'. 
• 50% is half (1/2), 25% is a quarter (1/4), and 10% is one-tenth (1/10). 
• To calculate 10% quickly, just drop the last zero or move the decimal one place to the left (e.g., 10% of ₹800 is ₹80).

tricks.title: ⚡ The 10% 'Zero-Drop' Rule
tricks.explanation: To find 10%, simply drop the last zero or move the decimal one place to the left.

tricks.title: 💰 5% 'Half of Ten' Method
tricks.explanation: Find 10% first, then cut that number in half.
tricks.example: To find 5% of ₹1,200: 10% is ₹120. Half of 120 is ₹60. Final = ₹60.

tricks.title: 🔄 The Reverse Percentage Hack
tricks.explanation: X% of Y is always equal to Y% of X. Switch the numbers to make it easier.
tricks.example: 16% of ₹25 is hard. 25% of ₹16 is easy! It's ₹4.

tricks.title: 🍕 The 25% 'Quarter' Cut
tricks.explanation: 25% is exactly one-quarter. Halve the number, then halve it again.
tricks.example: 25% of ₹400: Half is ₹200. Half again is ₹100. Final = ₹100.

tricks.title: 🚀 The 1% 'Two-Zero' Drop
tricks.explanation: To find 1%, drop the last two zeros or move the decimal two places left.

tricks.title: ➕ The 15% 'Tip' Trick
tricks.explanation: Find 10%, find 5% (half of that 10%), then add them together.

tricks.title: 🌓 The 50% 'Snap-Half'
tricks.explanation: 50% is just the number divided by 2. Always simplify to 'Half'.

tricks.title: 🔢 The 'Leading Digits' Multiply
tricks.explanation: If both numbers end in zero, just multiply the non-zero starting digits.

tricks.title: 👟 The 20% 'Double the 10' Trick
tricks.explanation: Find 10% and then just multiply it by 2.

tricks.title: 📉 The 90% 'Subtract 10' Rule
tricks.explanation: Instead of finding 90%, find 10% and subtract it from the total.

tricks.title: 🌟 The 75% 'Three-Quarters' Rule
tricks.explanation: Find 25% (half of a half) and multiply it by 3.

tricks.title: 🏛️ The 'Base 100' Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If the base is 100, the percentage is the actual number.
tricks.example: 13% of ₹100 is always ₹13. 87% of ₹100 is always ₹87.
